wording: description: "German VAT for tax year 2026, centred on the monthly or quarterly advance return (Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung, form USt 1 A) under standard taxation. Covers the 19% and 7% rates, including the 7% rate on restaurant and catering services (drinks excluded) from 1 January 2026; the small business limits of § 19 UStG (EUR 25,000 and EUR 100,000); monthly or quarterly filing (EUR 9,000 and EUR 2,000), the 10th-day deadline, the one-month extension and the 1/11 special prepayment; the annual return deadline; reverse charge under § 13b; the recapitulative statement; e-invoices (receiving since 2025, issuing by 2027 or 2028); late filing and late payment surcharges and interest; and the 2026 box numbers. Trigger on: Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung, UStVA, Vorsteuer, Kennzahl, Dauerfristverlängerung, Zusammenfassende Meldung, E-Rechnung, Säumniszuschlag, German VAT return. Out of scope: the annual return in detail, § 19, § 20 cash basis, partial exemption and OSS (de-vat-annual-and-special-schemes), e-invoice formats (germany-einvoice), income tax (de-income-tax)."
classification: Scope/companion routing only; no full excluded-specialist method asserted.

wording: - **Every business (Unternehmer) making taxable supplies in Germany** charges VAT and files advance returns, unless it is a small business under § 19 UStG or the tax office has released it (see "Deadlines and filing"). A business is anyone who carries on a commercial or professional activity independently: sole traders, freelancers, partnerships, GmbHs.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Small businesses (Kleinunternehmer).** A business based in Germany is exempt if its total turnover was not more than EUR 25,000 in the previous calendar year and does not exceed EUR 100,000 in the current year (§ 19(1) UStG). It charges no VAT, claims no input VAT, and the filing duties of § 18(1) to (4) UStG do not apply to it. It can waive the scheme; the waiver binds it for at least five calendar years (§ 19(3) UStG). The start-up year, the receipt that crosses the limit and the EU-wide scheme are in de-vat-annual-and-special-schemes.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Businesses established abroad** that make taxable supplies in Germany must register and file here unless the customer owes the tax under the reverse charge (§ 13b UStG) or the supplies go through the one-stop shop. See "Cross-border points".
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Customers who owe the tax.** A business (wherever it is established) or a legal person that receives a reverse-charge supply owes the VAT on it (§ 13b(5) UStG) and must file even if it makes no taxable supplies of its own (§ 18(4a) UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Out of scope here:** VAT groups (Organschaft), the margin schemes (§§ 25, 25a UStG), the flat rates for farmers and foresters (§ 24 UStG), and travel agents. Refer these.
classification: Scope/companion routing only; no full excluded-specialist method asserted.

wording:
**What is taxed.** Supplies of goods and services made in Germany for consideration by a business, intra-EU acquisitions of goods, imports, and private use of business assets (§ 3(1b) and (9a) UStG). The base is everything the customer pays, without the VAT itself.

**Foreign currency.** Convert the tax base and input VAT to euros using the BMF average rate for the month of the supply, or the month an advance payment is received before supply. A business permitted to use § 20 cash accounting uses the receipt month. A daily rate evidenced by a bank statement or exchange-rate list can be used only with the tax office's permission (§ 16(6) UStG). This is the standard-return route; the separate OSS exchange-rate rule is outside this method.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked. DE-B14 restores actual old §16(6) ordinary conversion. Currency-specific BMF monthly rate is an actual claimant input, not an invented fixed exchange rate.

wording: **Place of supply first, then the rate.** A service to a business is taxed where the customer is established (§ 3a(2) UStG). So a German consultant's service to a French company is not taxable in Germany, and a foreign supplier's service to a German business is taxed in Germany with the German customer owing the tax.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **Restaurant meals from 2026.** Food served in a restaurant or by a caterer is at 7% from 1 January 2026. Drinks stay at 19%. A bill must split the two. Where one price covers food and drinks (a buffet or all-inclusive deal), the tax office accepts 30% of the package price as the drinks share (UStAE 10.1(12)). For services in the night of 31 December 2025 to 1 January 2026, applying 19% is not challenged (BMF letter of 22 December 2025, no. 3).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **What the 7% rate covers, beyond goods.** § 12(2) UStG with Annex 2: food and the other Annex 2 goods, books and newspapers and their electronic editions, water, cut flowers and plants, dental technicians' work, admission to theatres, concerts, museums and zoos, and short-term letting of rooms and camping pitches. Services sold with a room that do not directly serve the letting (parking, internet) are not at the room rate (§ 12(2) no. 11 sentence 2). From 1 January 2026 breakfast food is a catering service at 7% under § 12(2) no. 15, with drinks at 19%. Where one package price covers the room and these services, the tax office accepts 15% of the package price as their share (UStAE 12.16(12) sentence 2, as amended by the BMF letter of 22 December 2025). Passenger transport is at 7% by rail without a distance limit, and by scheduled bus, taxi, cable car and ferry only within one municipality or where the journey is not more than 50 kilometres (§ 12(2) no. 10 UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked. Annex2 items remain tariff-classification-dependent; water and book exclusions are literal in own quote.

wording: **Solar at 0%.** The 0% rate is a rate, not an exemption, so the supplier keeps full input deduction. It covers supply, intra-EU acquisition, import and installation of modules, essential components and storage for systems on or near homes and public-benefit buildings; the conditions count as met up to 30 kWp registered in the Marktstammdatenregister (§ 12(3) UStG). Acquisitions at 0% go in Kz 90.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **Private use of business assets.** Withdrawal of business goods under § 3(1b) UStG is a deemed supply only where the goods or their components entitled the business to full or partial input deduction. Private use of an allocated business asset under § 3(9a) no. 1 UStG requires that the asset entitled the business to full or partial input deduction. For asset use, the exclusions in § 3(9a) no. 1 for § 15(1b) and § 15a(6a) also apply. Other free services under § 3(9a) no. 2 have their own rule. Report a taxable deemed supply at the applicable rate, normally in Kz 81. For a goods withdrawal the base is the purchase price of the item or an equivalent item, plus incidental costs, or otherwise cost, at the withdrawal date (§ 10(4) no. 1). For asset use it is the expenses that entitled the business to input deduction; acquisition or production costs of at least EUR 500 are spread over the applicable § 15a correction period (§ 10(4) no. 2), rather than using the income-tax list-price figure. A motor vehicle is not blocked for VAT: allocation and business use decide the deduction, and below 10% business use there is none.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked. DE-B12 corrects prior-input-entitlement gates, distinguishes components in goods withdrawal from asset itself for use, and preserves500costspreading threshold.

wording: **Input VAT (Vorsteuer).** A business deducts VAT charged by other businesses on an invoice that meets § 14 UStG, VAT on intra-EU acquisitions, import VAT that has arisen, and VAT it owes under the reverse charge (§ 15(1) UStG). No deduction for:
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - costs blocked by § 15(1a) UStG: gifts to one non-employee recipient costing more than EUR 50 in total in the year (then all of them, not only the excess), hunting, yachts, private living costs. Reasonable, evidenced business entertainment is NOT blocked for VAT (§ 15(1a) sentence 2 UStG): the 70% income-tax cut in § 4(5) sentence 1 no. 2 EStG does not reduce the VAT claim. Evidence means a written record of place, date, guests, reason and amount; in a restaurant, the reason and guests with the restaurant's invoice attached (§ 4(5) sentence 1 no. 2 sentences 2 and 3 EStG). From 2026 the food and drinks on the bill carry different rates;

wording: **Corrections and credit notes.** A Gutschrift (self-billing by the buyer, § 14(2) sentence 2 UStG) is an invoice and creates output tax for the supplier. A later change to the price (a discount, a cancellation, a credit note) is corrected in the period in which the change happens, not in the original period, by entering the change in the same box with a minus sign where it reduces the base (§ 17(1) UStG). Only where the fee has become uncollectible (§ 17(2) no. 1 UStG) is the reduction also shown in Kz 50 (line 51), or for input VAT in Kz 37 (line 52) (2026 form USt 1 A).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: | Bank fees, interest, loans, insurance premiums | Exempt or outside scope: no input VAT |
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: | Tax office, customs duty, chambers (IHK, HWK), broadcasting levy, statutory insurance, payroll and social contributions | Not a supply: leave out. Import VAT on a customs notice goes in Kz 62 |

wording: **Advance returns.** Filed electronically through ELSTER (https://www.elster.de) by the 10th day after the end of each period; the payment is due the same day (§ 18(1) UStG). Paper only with the tax office's permission to avoid hardship. A deadline on a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday moves to the next working day (§ 108(3) AO).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - Quarterly is the default (§ 18(2) UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - Monthly if the previous year's VAT was more than EUR 9,000.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - The tax office may release a business from advance returns if the previous year's VAT was not more than EUR 2,000. The annual return is still due.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - A business with a surplus of more than EUR 9,000 in the previous year may choose monthly by filing the January return by 10 February; the choice binds for the year (§ 18(2a) UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - New businesses: for tax years 2021 to 2026, a business that traded for only part of the previous year has that year's tax converted to a full-year figure, and a business starting in the current year uses its expected tax for this year (§ 18(2) last sentence UStG). The general rule of monthly filing in the first two years is set aside for these years. Shelf companies and bought dormant companies file monthly in the current and following year (§ 18(2) sentence 5 UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **One-month extension (Dauerfristverlängerung).** On application the tax office must extend the filing and payment deadline by one month, unless the tax looks at risk (§ 46 UStDV). Apply on form USt 1 H through ELSTER by the date the first affected return is due (§ 48(1) UStDV). A monthly filer must pay a special prepayment (Sondervorauszahlung) of 1/11 of the previous year's advance payments, by the due date of the first advance return of the year, 10 February (§ 47(1), § 48(2) UStDV). The base is the sum of the previous year's Kz 83 amounts plus the previous year's special prepayment credited in Kz 39 (2026 form instructions, lines 8 and 9). It is credited in Kz 39 of the last return of the year (§ 48(4) UStDV). A quarterly filer pays no special prepayment.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **Annual return.** Every business on standard taxation files an annual return for the calendar year (§ 18(3) UStG). For 2026 it is due 31 July 2027 (§ 149(2) AO), which is a Saturday, so Monday 2 August 2027 (§ 108(3) AO); if a tax adviser prepares it, by 29 February 2028 (§ 149(3) no. 4 AO). Any balance is due one month after the return is filed (§ 18(4) UStG). Detail: de-vat-annual-and-special-schemes.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: **Recapitulative statement (Zusammenfassende Meldung).** Sent to the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (https://www.bzst.de) by the 25th day after each month in which intra-EU supplies of goods were made; quarterly while those supplies stay at or below EUR 50,000 in the current and each of the four previous quarters (§ 18a(1) UStG). § 3a(2) services to EU businesses are reported by the 25th day after each quarter (§ 18a(2) UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - Receiving: since 1 January 2025 every business in Germany must be able to receive an e-invoice (a structured format such as XRechnung or ZUGFeRD), small businesses included. Receiving by e-mail needs no separate inbox (UStAE 14.1(5), BMF letter of 15 October 2025).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - Issuing: an invoice for a supply to another business must be an e-invoice where both are established in Germany (§ 14(2) sentence 2 no. 1 UStG). Transition (§ 27(38) UStG): for supplies made in 2025 and 2026, paper or another electronic format (with the customer's consent) is allowed until 31 December 2026; for supplies made in 2027, only if the issuer's 2026 total turnover was not more than EUR 800,000, or by EDI. For supplies from 1 January 2028 there is no relief.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - Small-amount invoices up to EUR 250, travel tickets and small businesses' invoices may always be issued as ordinary invoices (BMF letter of 15 October 2025, no. 22).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Late advance return.** The tax office may set a late filing surcharge (§ 152(1) AO). The 0.25% formula does not apply to monthly or quarterly returns or to the special prepayment; the amount is set by judgement, looking at how late, how often and how much tax (§ 152(8) AO). The cap is EUR 25,000 (§ 152(10) AO).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Late annual return.** 0.25% of the assessed tax less prepayments for each started month late, at least EUR 25 a month, rounded down to whole euros, at most EUR 25,000 (§ 152(5) and (10) AO). The surcharge is compulsory if the return is not filed within 14 months after the year ends (for 2026, by 29 February 2028, which is also the tax-adviser deadline), unless the deadline was extended, the tax is nil or negative, or the tax does not exceed the prepayments (§ 152(2) and (3) AO).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Late payment (Säumniszuschlag).** 1% for each started month on the overdue tax rounded down to a multiple of EUR 50 (§ 240(1) AO). No surcharge if the payment is no more than 3 days late, except for payment in cash or by cheque (§ 240(3) AO with § 224(2) no. 1 AO). A bank transfer counts on the day the tax office's account is credited (§ 224(2) no. 2 AO). It runs on advance payments, the special prepayment and the annual balance.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Interest (§ 233a AO).** Where the annual assessment differs from the prepayments, the difference carries interest of 0.15% per full month, from 15 months after the year ends (for 2026, from 1 April 2028) until the assessment takes effect (§ 233a(2) AO, § 238(1a) AO). The amount is rounded down to a multiple of EUR 50 (§ 238(2) AO). Advance payments themselves carry no § 233a interest (§ 233a(1) sentence 2 AO).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Fines** for VAT not paid on time (§ 26a UStG) are covered in de-vat-annual-and-special-schemes.
classification: Scope/companion routing only; no full excluded-specialist method asserted.

wording: - **Services received from abroad.** A § 3a(2) service from an EU business: base Kz 46, tax Kz 47, input Kz 67; the tax arises at the end of the period in which the service was performed (§ 13b(1) UStG). Other services and works supplies from a business established abroad (including non-EU): Kz 84 and 85; the tax arises when the invoice is issued, at the latest at the end of the month after the supply (§ 13b(2) no. 1 UStG). A fully taxable business pays and deducts the same amount.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Services supplied abroad.** A § 3a(2) service to a business in another EU state is not taxable in Germany: Kz 21, the recapitulative statement, and an invoice noting that the customer owes the tax. To a business outside the EU: Kz 45.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Goods.** Intra-EU supplies to a customer with a valid VAT ID are tax-free with input deduction (Kz 41), with transport evidence. Arrival in the other member state is presumed where the supplier transported the goods and holds two consistent documents from parties independent of each other and of both sides, or, where the customer transported them, also holds a Gelangensbestätigung (entry certificate) delivered by the customer by the 10th day of the month after the supply (§ 17a(1) UStDV, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ustdv_1980/__17a.html); otherwise the evidence rules of § 17b UStDV apply; exports outside the EU go in Kz 43. Acquisitions from EU suppliers are self-assessed (Kz 89 or 93, input Kz 61). Import VAT is charged by customs and deducted in Kz 62.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Domestic reverse charge.** Construction services (where the customer itself regularly supplies construction services), building cleaning, scrap metal, gold, mobile phones, tablets, consoles, chips and Annex 4 metals at EUR 5,000 or more per transaction, gas through the natural-gas network and electricity from a supplier abroad, emission allowances, and the other categories listed in § 13b(2) UStG: the business customer owes the tax. Building cleaning applies only where the customer itself supplies cleaning services. For the EUR 5,000 test a later reduction of the fee is ignored (§ 13b(2) no. 10 UStG) (§ 13b(2) and (5) UStG). The supplier reports the sale in Kz 60.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording: - **Distance sales to EU consumers.** For a supplier established in only one member state, Germany, up to EUR 10,000 a year EU-wide (goods and electronic services together, previous and current year), German VAT applies; above it, the customer's country's VAT, usually through the one-stop shop (§ 3c(4) UStG). One EU-wide total, not per country. A business may waive the limit; the waiver binds for at least two calendar years (§ 3c(4) UStG). See de-vat-annual-and-special-schemes.
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked. DE-B13 adds own one-Member-State establishment gate. Exact10k boundary still inclusive.

wording: - **Foreign businesses.** A business established abroad that makes taxable supplies in Germany not covered by the reverse charge registers and files like a German business. A foreign business with no German filing duty recovers German input VAT through the refund procedure (§ 18(9) UStG).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked.

wording:
### Example 1: An IT consultant's monthly return, with a late payment

Anna is a freelance IT consultant in Berlin on standard taxation. Her 2025 VAT was above EUR 9,000, so she files monthly in 2026 without an extension. For March 2026 she has:
- fees from German clients of EUR 20,000 net, at 19%: EUR 3,800 VAT, Kz 81;
- fees from a French company of EUR 5,000 for consulting: not taxable in Germany, Kz 21 and the recapitulative statement, no VAT;
- German purchase invoices showing EUR 1,140 VAT: Kz 66;
- a US software subscription of EUR 200 billed by the US entity: Kz 84 EUR 200, Kz 85 EUR 38;
- online advertising of EUR 1,000 billed by an Irish company: Kz 46 EUR 1,000, Kz 47 EUR 190.

The reverse-charge tax of EUR 228 is also her input VAT in Kz 67. Output VAT is EUR 4,028, input VAT EUR 1,368, so Kz 83 is EUR 2,660. The return and payment are due Friday 10 April 2026. Her transfer reaches the tax office on Tuesday 14 April, 4 days late, past the 3-day grace period. The surcharge is 1% of EUR 2,650 (EUR 2,660 rounded down to a multiple of 50) for one started month: EUR 26.50.

```oa-check
name: IT consultant, March 2026 advance return with reverse charge and a late payment
inputs:
  domestic_net: 20000
  eu_service_sale: 5000
  domestic_input_vat: 1140
  non_eu_software: 200
  eu_advertising: 1000
  standard_rate: 19
  months_late: 1
steps:
  - kz81_tax: pct(domestic_net, standard_rate)
  - kz85_tax: pct(non_eu_software, standard_rate)
  - kz47_tax: pct(eu_advertising, standard_rate)
  - output_vat_line37: kz81_tax + kz85_tax + kz47_tax
  - kz67_input: kz85_tax + kz47_tax
  - input_vat_total: domestic_input_vat + kz67_input
  - kz83: output_vat_line37 - input_vat_total
  - overdue_rounded: floor(kz83 / 50) * 50
  - late_payment_surcharge: pct(overdue_rounded, 1) * months_late
expected:
  kz81_tax: 3800
  kz85_tax: 38
  kz47_tax: 190
  output_vat_line37: 4028
  kz67_input: 228
  input_vat_total: 1368
  kz83: 2660
  overdue_rounded: 2650
  late_payment_surcharge: 26.50
```
classification: Original current executable case; all amounts stipulated/computed, not amounts quoted as enacted law. Own fresh arithmetic and original-case variants in writer-checks.

wording:
### Example 2: A restaurant's December return, buffet at two rates and the special prepayment

A restaurant GmbH files monthly with the one-month extension. Its 2025 advance returns showed Kz 83 amounts of EUR 61,000 in total, and its 2025 special prepayment of EUR 5,000 was credited in December 2025. The base for 2026 is EUR 66,000, so the 2026 special prepayment is EUR 6,000, declared on form USt 1 H and paid by 10 February 2026.

In December 2026 it sells only buffet packages, food and drinks for one price, for EUR 127,330 gross. Using the 30% drinks share (UStAE 10.1(12)), EUR 38,199 is drinks at 19% (net EUR 32,100, VAT EUR 6,099, Kz 81) and EUR 89,131 is food at 7% (net EUR 83,300, VAT EUR 5,831, Kz 86). Output VAT is EUR 11,930. Input VAT on invoices is EUR 4,200 (Kz 66), leaving EUR 7,730 in line 48. December is the last period, so the EUR 6,000 special prepayment is credited in Kz 39, and Kz 83 is EUR 1,730. With the extension it is due 10 February 2027. Had the whole price been taxed at 19%, as before 2026, output VAT would have been EUR 20,330.

```oa-check
name: Restaurant, December 2026 return with a 30% drinks share and the special prepayment credit
inputs:
  kz83_2025_total: 61000
  svz_2025: 5000
  package_gross: 127330
  drinks_share_pct: 30
  input_vat: 4200
steps:
  - svz_base: kz83_2025_total + svz_2025
  - svz_2026: svz_base / 11
  - drinks_gross: pct(package_gross, drinks_share_pct)
  - food_gross: package_gross - drinks_gross
  - drinks_net_kz81: drinks_gross * 100 / 119
  - food_net_kz86: food_gross * 100 / 107
  - drinks_vat: drinks_gross - drinks_net_kz81
  - food_vat: food_gross - food_net_kz86
  - output_vat: drinks_vat + food_vat
  - line48: output_vat - input_vat
  - kz83_december: line48 - svz_2026
  - output_vat_all_at_19: package_gross * 19 / 119
expected:
  svz_base: 66000
  svz_2026: 6000
  drinks_gross: 38199
  food_gross: 89131
  drinks_net_kz81: 32100
  food_net_kz86: 83300
  drinks_vat: 6099
  food_vat: 5831
  output_vat: 11930
  line48: 7730
  kz83_december: 1730
  output_vat_all_at_19: 20330
```
classification: Original current executable case; all amounts stipulated/computed, not amounts quoted as enacted law. Own fresh arithmetic and original-case variants in writer-checks.

wording:
1. Is the business on standard taxation, or a small business under § 19 UStG? What was total turnover in 2025, and what is it so far in 2026?
2. Monthly or quarterly, and is there a one-month extension? If monthly with the extension, was the 2026 special prepayment declared and paid, and is this the last return of the year?
3. For each foreign supplier: which legal entity issued the invoice, and where is it established? This decides Kz 46 and 47 against Kz 84 and 85.
4. For each EU customer: is there a valid VAT ID, and was it checked with the Bundeszentralamt für Steuern?
5. Any exempt income (residential rent, medical, education, insurance, financial services)? If so, input VAT needs apportioning.
6. For restaurants and caterers: do the till and invoices split food from drinks, and are there package prices?
classification: Intake facts that determine the quoted methods.

wording: **While facts are missing (OpenAccountants working practice, not a legal rule).** Use these defaults and say so in the working paper: an unknown rate on a sale is 19%; an unknown VAT status of a purchase is not deductible; an EU customer with no confirmed VAT ID is a consumer; an unknown business share (vehicle, phone, home office) gives no deduction; a software or advertising supplier whose billing entity is unknown goes in Kz 84 and 85; entertainment without the written record is blocked. If only a bank statement was supplied, record for the reviewer that input VAT claims must be checked against invoices meeting § 14 UStG, that the § 33 UStDV small-amount relief was used only up to EUR 250, and that every reverse-charge line matches the supplier's invoice.
classification: Express OpenAccountants conservative working-paper defaults, not enacted legal classifications. Never used to prove customer status from IBAN or a brand.

wording: Not yet confirmed: that the EUR 50 gift limit is counted by calendar year for VAT (UStAE 15.6(4) was not read for this version; the income-tax text counts by financial year); that the entertainment receipt must be machine-produced and signed by the host (an administrative rule, not in § 4(5) EStG); which tax office handles a foreign business, by country (the Umsatzsteuerzuständigkeitsverordnung was not read for this version); the rounding rule for whole-euro tax bases on the advance return (the 2026 instructions say whole euros but not whether to round or cut off the cents).
classification: Operative own primary/official administrative rule; exact original-language quote and actual read date linked. Exact retained reservation: quoted EStG uses Wirtschaftsjahr; unacquired UStAE15.6(4) calendar-year question remains. No silent resolution.
